newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Zedillo vows to fight political attacks.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Zedillo vows to fight political attacks.

text.p: Mexico's President Ernesto Zedillo vowed to respond to political attacks, saying he has the right to speak out before upcoming key mid-term elections, newspapers reported on Sunday.
Zedillo has come under attack from opposition politicians, who say the representative of the long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) should rise above the fray before the July 6 votes.
Mexicans will vote for a new lower house in Congress, as well as part of the Senate, governors in six states and the mayor of Mexico City.
Responding to demands he stay out of the fight, Zedillo said democracy starts with "truth and tolerance."

"Those who base their political propaganda in attacking the government are lacking truth and tolerance. They have the right, and I respect this right, but at the same time they are demanding that the government remain silent before these attacks," Zedillo said in a statement released late on Saturday.
The president of the PRD, Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador, attacked Zedillo in a letter released late on Saturday, exhorting him to act like a "statesman."
"What happend to the healthy distance from your party that you promised," Lopez Obrador wrote. "Was that pure demagoguery?"

On Friday Zedillo attacked pre-election publicity by opposition parties as attempts to fool the public. He said they were "using publicity like people trying to sell potato chips, beer and soda pop to tell people that like this they can resolve their problems.
Zedillo's PRI is in in a tough battle with opposition conservative National Action Party (PAN) and the left-wing Party of the Democractic Revolution (PRD) before the July 6 elections.
All three parties, and some smaller ones, flooded television and radio with hard-hitting advertisements.
Recent polls placed the PRD ahead in the vote for the mayor's job in Mexico City, while the outcome in Congress was less clear.
